rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes HPHT treatment of a dual-phase Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy, while the target paper uses MD simulation of uniaxial tensile loading on single-crystal FeNiCrMn. These are entirely different kinds of interventions (processing vs. mechanical testing simulation).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies HPHT conditions (6 GPa, 1473 K, 2 h), whereas the target paper uses MD tensile tests at 10–600 K and strain rates of 10^8–10^10 s^-1. The regimes are completely different (high-pressure processing vs. cryogenic-to-elevated temperature mechanical testing).
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes coherent interface dislocation transfer and hierarchical deformation modes in a dual-phase alloy, while the target paper describes dislocation nucleation at vacancy clusters and plasticity via Shockley partials and stacking faults in a single-phase FCC HEA. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts simultaneous doubling of strength and ductility to ~1150 MPa and ~36%, whereas the target paper predicts yield stress anisotropy, temperature softening, and strain-rate insensitivity. The properties, directions, and magnitudes are entirely different.
